review_text: **SCAMMING VISITORS** My wife and I were trying to locate the PUBLIC mangroves near the hotel. We pulled up outside the Anantara hotel to ask for directions and the valet informed us that we can access the mangrove from the hotel and that we pay him AED30 in cash. He was quite adamant that payment had to be in cash as he mentioned it 4 times between the time of my getting out the car and collecting my belongings. Once we entered the hotel we figured out this was not where we wanted to be. The only thing they had was kayaking which we did not want to do. I asked the valet to bring my car and for a refund as it had been less than 5 minutes and he refused despite my protest. I then went inside to speak to management to explain the situation and to my surprise I was met with the same response. They refused to share the general managers work email address or any other email for me to issue a formal complaint which I found extremely bizarre. One of the staff offered to speak to the valet for me but I realised this was only a tactic to have me move away from the reception area as he changed his tone as soon as we reached outside. One of the hotel managers (who refused to give his name) then came and within seconds my wife and I were surrounded by several male staff and tried to intimidate us. I expressed my shock and distaste at the fact that a renowned hotel such as Anantara would be trying to scam residents out of AED30 for parking. The manager then came to my car door and said “do we have a problem?” In a thuggish manner. I am absolutely appalled and disgusted. The most shocking thing is rather than letting us know there is free public parking less than 1 minute down the road, they try to con residents out of money. After arguing for 20mins I finally got my money back and the manager told me to “get out of his hotel”. Whilst speaking with the staff inside there was another hotel visitor trying to get a refund for her stay due to the poor service and quality. Reading a lot of other reviews it seems this hotel has a lot to figure out. I am 100% certain this was not an isolated incident, you get the feeling this is something they do often and for a hotel which supposedly carries such a high standard and prides themselves on “luxury”, trying to scam residents and tourists is not a good look.
owner_answer:
Dear Toseef Butt,

Thank you for bringing your concerns to our attention regarding your recent visit to Anantara Eastern Mangroves Hotel. We sincerely apologize for any confusion or inconvenience you experienced during your interaction with our valet parking service.

Please allow me to clarify that our valet parking service is available for hotel guests and visitors utilizing our facilities. However, we do not charge hotel guests for valet parking. We regret any miscommunication that may have occurred regarding this matter, and we will ensure that our valet team provides clear and accurate information to all visitors in the future.

Additionally, regarding your inquiry about accessing the public mangroves, I would like to clarify that kayaking activities at our location are managed by a separate company. While we do not oversee parking arrangements for non-hotel guests participating in activities such as Kayaking, we will communicate your feedback to the relevant parties for further review and improvement.

We take all guest feedback seriously and are committed to providing a positive experience for all visitors to Anantara Eastern Mangroves Hotel.  

Thank you for bringing this to our attention, and we hope to have the opportunity to restore your confidence in our services in the future.

Warm regards,

Nicola Mandolini
Hotel Manager

Terrible terrible experience.

Extremely disappointing customer service and poor coordination.

I had a very frustrating experience with them, mainly due to their call center’s incompetence and lack of accountability.

I had a valid voucher and called the customer service center to ask how to book a session. I was told I could either book in person or that they could reserve the session for me over the phone. To avoid inconvenience, I chose the phone option. Given my doubts of their incompetence, I called multiple times to confirm that my session was booked and was reassured each time that my request had been noted and processed.

On the day of the session, I arrived only to find out that nothing had been booked at all. I wasted a significant amount of time going back and forth between the venue reception and the call center, and no solution was reached.

To be fair, the venue reception staff were polite and professional and offered a complimentary session and a reschedule. However, by that point my experience was already ruined, and I declined.

The call center experience was unacceptable: during one call, an agent read a note that clearly stated my request (“Book L2 session…”), but after being put on hold for a long time and calling again, I was told that I must have “heard wrong.” This is despite the fact that I had called more than once specifically to confirm the booking.

Now, instead of enjoying the experience I planned for, I’m forced into a long, tedious refund process for something that failed due to their internal mismanagement.

Great facility, but severely undermined by an unreliable and inconsistent call center. I would not recommend booking anything through phone support.

Now, instead of enjoying the experience I planned for, I’m forced into a long, tedious refund process for something that failed due to their internal mismanagement.

Great facility, but severely undermined by an unreliable and inconsistent call center. I would not recommend booking anything through phone support.

review_text:
Ferrari World Abu Dhabi is a dream destination for speed junkies and automotive enthusiasts alike. One of the best parts of the experience is that the entire park is indoors, providing a comfortable, climate-controlled environment to enjoy world-class thrills regardless of the weather outside.

The absolute standout ride is Formula Rossa. As the fastest roller coaster in the world, its lightning-fast acceleration is something you have to feel to believe; it is truly the ultimate adrenaline rush.

For those seeking sheer intensity, Flying Aces is incredibly thrilling, featuring one of the world's highest roller coaster loops.

I also highly recommend Mission Ferrari, which stands out as a brilliantly interactive and immersive roller coaster that blends physical drops with high-tech storytelling.

Even the Turbo track provides a great ride, adding to the variety of the park.

Beyond the heart-pounding attractions, the atmosphere is elevated by the stunning display of Ferrari car models. Seeing the evolution and craftsmanship of these iconic machines up close makes the visit all the more impressive. Whether you are there for the record-breaking speeds or the Italian luxury, Ferrari World is a top-tier attraction that shouldn't be missed.

review_text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience – Total Waste of Money

I had one of the worst theme park experiences of my life at Ferrari World Abu Dhabi, and I strongly regret coming here.

I visited with my family who came all the way to Dubai to see me, including my young siblings who were extremely excited about Ferrari World. I spent over 2,200 AED just on tickets, expecting a world-class experience. What no one tells you — and what should be clearly mentioned — is that waiting times are absolutely insane: 2 to 5 HOURS per ride.

When we arrived, all fast pass tickets were already sold out. I went to the information desk and politely asked if they could help us with just TWO fast pass tickets for my young siblings, explaining that they might never get the chance to visit again. The answer was a flat NO, no empathy, no effort to help, nothing.

As a result, we managed to ride only ONE roller coaster after waiting 2.5 hours. When we tried to go to other rides, the queues were 3 to 4 hours long. This is completely unacceptable and honestly insane for a paid attraction at this price level.

My younger siblings were heartbroken and disappointed, and as a family we felt cheated. This place is severely overcrowded, clearly with no limit on the number of people allowed inside, and the management seems to care only about selling tickets, not about visitor experience.

Unless you buy fast pass tickets WELL IN ADVANCE, do NOT come here. Otherwise, you will spend your entire day standing in lines and walking around doing nothing.

Ironically, the best time to visit is probably summer, because right now it feels like they are just taking people’s money for nothing. For the price paid, this experience was absolutely not worth it.

I do NOT recommend Ferrari World to anyone without fast pass tickets. Save your money or go somewhere that actually values its guests.

review_text:
It's a straight up money printing machine to make up for the otherwise lackluster Abu Dhabi. They sell unlimited tickets resulting in 3-4 hrs of waittimes for the main rides and 30mins - 1.5 hrs wait times for all the other decent ones. A full days pass of 375 AED and you are lucky enough to get in 3 rides all day. Not to mention it's a weekday and I'm terrified of what the waittimes are on the weekends.

Ferrari World simply sucks and is overhyped. Please look into other better options like the other theme parks in Dubai. Surely, you might not have the World's fastest coaster but you can enjoy a slightly slower coaster multiple times and get great bang for your buck.

Edit: The cafes inside are overpriced compared to anywhere on the yas island. You're better off entering the yas mall food court for good food. Not to mention there are wait times of upto 1 hr to place your food order in a few joints inside. The main rollercoaster was closed for about an hour for 'maintenance' extending the wait time to approximately 5 hrs. You're better off spending your money and time elsewhere in UAE, there is plenty more to see here

If you are gonna come to Ferrari World, make sure you come in the middle of summer when there is no one around. But again, there is no guarantee that the money hungry folks of FW will have the main attractions working.

name: Ferrari World Yas Island, Abu Dhabi
review_text:
Ferrari World Abu Dhabi is a dream destination for speed junkies and automotive enthusiasts alike. One of the best parts of the experience is that the entire park is indoors, providing a comfortable, climate-controlled environment to enjoy world-class thrills regardless of the weather outside.

The absolute standout ride is Formula Rossa. As the fastest roller coaster in the world, its lightning-fast acceleration is something you have to feel to believe; it is truly the ultimate adrenaline rush.

For those seeking sheer intensity, Flying Aces is incredibly thrilling, featuring one of the world's highest roller coaster loops.

I also highly recommend Mission Ferrari, which stands out as a brilliantly interactive and immersive roller coaster that blends physical drops with high-tech storytelling.

Even the Turbo track provides a great ride, adding to the variety of the park.

Beyond the heart-pounding attractions, the atmosphere is elevated by the stunning display of Ferrari car models. Seeing the evolution and craftsmanship of these iconic machines up close makes the visit all the more impressive. Whether you are there for the record-breaking speeds or the Italian luxury, Ferrari World is a top-tier attraction that shouldn't be missed.

review_text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience – Total Waste of Money

I had one of the worst theme park experiences of my life at Ferrari World Abu Dhabi, and I strongly regret coming here.

I visited with my family who came all the way to Dubai to see me, including my young siblings who were extremely excited about Ferrari World. I spent over 2,200 AED just on tickets, expecting a world-class experience. What no one tells you — and what should be clearly mentioned — is that waiting times are absolutely insane: 2 to 5 HOURS per ride.

When we arrived, all fast pass tickets were already sold out. I went to the information desk and politely asked if they could help us with just TWO fast pass tickets for my young siblings, explaining that they might never get the chance to visit again. The answer was a flat NO, no empathy, no effort to help, nothing.

As a result, we managed to ride only ONE roller coaster after waiting 2.5 hours. When we tried to go to other rides, the queues were 3 to 4 hours long. This is completely unacceptable and honestly insane for a paid attraction at this price level.

My younger siblings were heartbroken and disappointed, and as a family we felt cheated. This place is severely overcrowded, clearly with no limit on the number of people allowed inside, and the management seems to care only about selling tickets, not about visitor experience.

Unless you buy fast pass tickets WELL IN ADVANCE, do NOT come here. Otherwise, you will spend your entire day standing in lines and walking around doing nothing.

Ironically, the best time to visit is probably summer, because right now it feels like they are just taking people’s money for nothing. For the price paid, this experience was absolutely not worth it.

I do NOT recommend Ferrari World to anyone without fast pass tickets. Save your money or go somewhere that actually values its guests.

review_text:
It's a straight up money printing machine to make up for the otherwise lackluster Abu Dhabi. They sell unlimited tickets resulting in 3-4 hrs of waittimes for the main rides and 30mins - 1.5 hrs wait times for all the other decent ones. A full days pass of 375 AED and you are lucky enough to get in 3 rides all day. Not to mention it's a weekday and I'm terrified of what the waittimes are on the weekends.

Ferrari World simply sucks and is overhyped. Please look into other better options like the other theme parks in Dubai. Surely, you might not have the World's fastest coaster but you can enjoy a slightly slower coaster multiple times and get great bang for your buck.

Edit: The cafes inside are overpriced compared to anywhere on the yas island. You're better off entering the yas mall food court for good food. Not to mention there are wait times of upto 1 hr to place your food order in a few joints inside. The main rollercoaster was closed for about an hour for 'maintenance' extending the wait time to approximately 5 hrs. You're better off spending your money and time elsewhere in UAE, there is plenty more to see here

If you are gonna come to Ferrari World, make sure you come in the middle of summer when there is no one around. But again, there is no guarantee that the money hungry folks of FW will have the main attractions working.

name: Ferrari World Yas Island, Abu Dhabi
review_text:
Ferrari World Abu Dhabi is a dream destination for speed junkies and automotive enthusiasts alike. One of the best parts of the experience is that the entire park is indoors, providing a comfortable, climate-controlled environment to enjoy world-class thrills regardless of the weather outside.

The absolute standout ride is Formula Rossa. As the fastest roller coaster in the world, its lightning-fast acceleration is something you have to feel to believe; it is truly the ultimate adrenaline rush.

For those seeking sheer intensity, Flying Aces is incredibly thrilling, featuring one of the world's highest roller coaster loops.

I also highly recommend Mission Ferrari, which stands out as a brilliantly interactive and immersive roller coaster that blends physical drops with high-tech storytelling.

Even the Turbo track provides a great ride, adding to the variety of the park.

Beyond the heart-pounding attractions, the atmosphere is elevated by the stunning display of Ferrari car models. Seeing the evolution and craftsmanship of these iconic machines up close makes the visit all the more impressive. Whether you are there for the record-breaking speeds or the Italian luxury, Ferrari World is a top-tier attraction that shouldn't be missed.

review_text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience – Total Waste of Money

I had one of the worst theme park experiences of my life at Ferrari World Abu Dhabi, and I strongly regret coming here.

I visited with my family who came all the way to Dubai to see me, including my young siblings who were extremely excited about Ferrari World. I spent over 2,200 AED just on tickets, expecting a world-class experience. What no one tells you — and what should be clearly mentioned — is that waiting times are absolutely insane: 2 to 5 HOURS per ride.

When we arrived, all fast pass tickets were already sold out. I went to the information desk and politely asked if they could help us with just TWO fast pass tickets for my young siblings, explaining that they might never get the chance to visit again. The answer was a flat NO, no empathy, no effort to help, nothing.

As a result, we managed to ride only ONE roller coaster after waiting 2.5 hours. When we tried to go to other rides, the queues were 3 to 4 hours long. This is completely unacceptable and honestly insane for a paid attraction at this price level.

My younger siblings were heartbroken and disappointed, and as a family we felt cheated. This place is severely overcrowded, clearly with no limit on the number of people allowed inside, and the management seems to care only about selling tickets, not about visitor experience.

Unless you buy fast pass tickets WELL IN ADVANCE, do NOT come here. Otherwise, you will spend your entire day standing in lines and walking around doing nothing.

Ironically, the best time to visit is probably summer, because right now it feels like they are just taking people’s money for nothing. For the price paid, this experience was absolutely not worth it.

I do NOT recommend Ferrari World to anyone without fast pass tickets. Save your money or go somewhere that actually values its guests.

They sell unlimited tickets resulting in 3-4 hrs of waittimes for the main rides and 30mins - 1.5 hrs wait times for all the other decent ones. A full days pass of 375 AED and you are lucky enough to get in 3 rides all day. Not to mention it's a weekday and I'm terrified of what the waittimes are on the weekends.

You're better off spending your money and time elsewhere in UAE, there is plenty more to see here

name: Al Hudayriat Island
review_text:
Al Hudayriat Island has quickly become one of my favourite places in Abu Dhabi. It’s the kind of destination where you feel an instant shift the moment you arrive — open spaces, wide skies, and that refreshing island breeze that makes everything feel lighter. Whether you’re going for a walk, a bike ride, or just a peaceful break from the city, the whole area feels thoughtfully designed and beautifully maintained.

The beach is clean and spacious, with stunning views, soft sand, and plenty of room to relax without feeling crowded. I love how the island blends nature with modern facilities: cafés, food trucks, sports areas, running and cycling tracks, and shaded seating all come together so effortlessly. It’s family-friendly, active-friendly, and perfect for solo visits too.

What really stands out is the atmosphere — calm, uplifting, and full of life at the same time. You see people exercising, families enjoying the beach, friends gathering for a casual evening, and it all adds to the energy of the place. It’s one of the rare spots that truly offers something for everyone.

Whether you want an active day or a quiet escape, Al Hudayriat Island delivers every time. A must-visit in Abu Dhabi.

query: rays-grill,Rays Grill, Corniche, Abu Dhabi
name: Ray's Grill
review_text:
From the moment we walked into Ray’s Grill, we knew we were in for something special. The ambiance was warm and inviting, and the menu was full of tempting options, each dish showcasing fresh ingredients and creative flavors.

But what truly set our experience apart was the service. Alam, our server, was nothing short of amazing. Attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely lovely, he made us feel like VIPs from start to finish. His recommendations were spot-on, and his passion for both the food and the guests was evident in every interaction.

The food was beautifully presented and absolutely delicious. Each bite was perfectly seasoned and cooked to perfection, and it was clear the kitchen took great pride in their craft. We left Ray’s Grill feeling more than satisfied – it was a memorable experience we’ll be talking about for a long time.

If you’re looking for a place with outstanding food and the warmest service (be sure to ask for Alam!), Ray’s Grill is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

review_text: My boyfriend and I went to Ray’s Grill to celebrate something special, but unfortunately, the food ruined our night. When I mentioned this to the waitress and demonstrated how difficult it was to cut the steak, she attributed it to our order of 500 grams, even though it appeared to be closer to 300 grams or less. review_text:
We liked this place overall.

The thing that bummed us the most about this place was the staff's behavior at the entry gate. They were checking bags and the checking lady in the extreme right line was super rude. She not only made us throw all food we had, but also spoke in a very condescending tone and humiliated us out of the queue.

I requested her to let us keep a piece of cake we got for our son, but NO, she asked us to throw that too. How else would food vendors inside the park earn if we get our son's favorite cake inside the park, even if it were to make sure he's not famished in the first half of the day.

I am all in for compliance and following rules, just be a little flexible when it comes to kids and a small piece of cake ain't hurting anybody. Toddlers are hard to console when something they're looking forward to, gets thrown in the bin.

Nevertheless, we started with the dolphin show. Very average. Kudos to the dolphins, but the stage presenters really need to up their game. No one could understand a word they said. The dolphin show at the Dubai Dolphinarium was wayyyyyyyyy better. Also, what's with the reserved seating at the auditorium ? You wouldn't give reserved seats to folks with toddlers even if they reach the auditorium well before the show, but quick pass owners get reserved seating even at the last minute? I understand quick pass folks getting quick access , but why give them reserved seating ?

Anyway, endless ocean and Arctic circle is beautifully maintained at Sea World. We loved the penguin area and how everybody gets a chance to get close to the penguins in a habitat that suits them.

Loved the Polar region too, the Walrus was the big showstopper at the park. Maybe do something about the stench in that area ?

Food at Seaworld is pretty expensive, but the café near the penguin area is particularly goood and has good value for money.

We missed the mermaid show and there was just 1 show in the entire day. It was a bummer to not have caught that show. Felt like there could be announcements in the park or displays that showed timings and venues to these things..

The amazing 360 displays at the center of the park enthrall you and present a spectacular view of the shows.

We kept checking with various staff members about the "Pick a pearl" bit, but we failed to get any clarity on what it was all about and left without taking that experience ultimately.

Seaworld does seem promising for a future visit. I'd like to give it another go in the future, hoping for a much better experience next time 🤞

review_text:
Major safety failure: no staff or security response to threats during a family show

We attended a show here with our two children (aged 4 and 7). What happened raised serious concerns about guest safety and the venue’s ability to manage incidents inside the amphitheater.

Seating was unassigned and guests were taking any available seats. I entered first and seated our child in a single free seat. No one indicated that the seat was reserved or being held. When my husband arrived a few minutes later, he sat with our child (the child remained in the same seat, sitting on his lap). At that point, a nearby group suddenly claimed the seat was being held.

A man from that group arrived about a minute before the end of the show and immediately began shouting at my husband, claiming the seat and making direct physical threats, all while standing next to our child. The situation continued despite the show being almost finished.

Most concerning was the complete lack of response from the venue. There was no visible staff or security presence in the amphitheater, and no intervention at any point. I was forced to leave one of our children alone and go into the corridor to try to find help, yet no assistance came. Even after the show ended, the aggressive behaviour continued and we left feeling unsafe.

The impact on our family was significant. Our children were frightened and distressed, and the rest of our day was affected by stress and anxiety after what should have been a normal family outing.

When we approached reception ourselves, we were told to stand in a queue and submit a complaint. This is not an appropriate response when guests have been threatened and children are involved. Later, we received an official reply describing the incident as a “misunderstanding.” We strongly disagree: physical threats, lack of intervention, and distressed children are not a misunderstanding.

We expect a formal follow-up from management and clear action to ensure visible staff and security presence, proper escalation procedures, and active monitoring during family shows. Without these measures, families cannot feel safe attending events at this venue.

review_text:
We liked this place overall.

The thing that bummed us the most about this place was the staff's behavior at the entry gate. They were checking bags and the checking lady in the extreme right line was super rude. She not only made us throw all food we had, but also spoke in a very condescending tone and humiliated us out of the queue.

I requested her to let us keep a piece of cake we got for our son, but NO, she asked us to throw that too. How else would food vendors inside the park earn if we get our son's favorite cake inside the park, even if it were to make sure he's not famished in the first half of the day.

I am all in for compliance and following rules, just be a little flexible when it comes to kids and a small piece of cake ain't hurting anybody. Toddlers are hard to console when something they're looking forward to, gets thrown in the bin.

Nevertheless, we started with the dolphin show. Very average. Kudos to the dolphins, but the stage presenters really need to up their game. No one could understand a word they said. The dolphin show at the Dubai Dolphinarium was wayyyyyyyyy better. Also, what's with the reserved seating at the auditorium ? You wouldn't give reserved seats to folks with toddlers even if they reach the auditorium well before the show, but quick pass owners get reserved seating even at the last minute? I understand quick pass folks getting quick access , but why give them reserved seating ?

Anyway, endless ocean and Arctic circle is beautifully maintained at Sea World. We loved the penguin area and how everybody gets a chance to get close to the penguins in a habitat that suits them.

Loved the Polar region too, the Walrus was the big showstopper at the park. Maybe do something about the stench in that area ?

Food at Seaworld is pretty expensive, but the café near the penguin area is particularly goood and has good value for money.

We missed the mermaid show and there was just 1 show in the entire day. It was a bummer to not have caught that show. Felt like there could be announcements in the park or displays that showed timings and venues to these things..

The amazing 360 displays at the center of the park enthrall you and present a spectacular view of the shows.

We kept checking with various staff members about the "Pick a pearl" bit, but we failed to get any clarity on what it was all about and left without taking that experience ultimately.

Seaworld does seem promising for a future visit. I'd like to give it another go in the future, hoping for a much better experience next time 🤞

review_text:
Major safety failure: no staff or security response to threats during a family show

We attended a show here with our two children (aged 4 and 7). What happened raised serious concerns about guest safety and the venue’s ability to manage incidents inside the amphitheater.

Seating was unassigned and guests were taking any available seats. I entered first and seated our child in a single free seat. No one indicated that the seat was reserved or being held. When my husband arrived a few minutes later, he sat with our child (the child remained in the same seat, sitting on his lap). At that point, a nearby group suddenly claimed the seat was being held.

A man from that group arrived about a minute before the end of the show and immediately began shouting at my husband, claiming the seat and making direct physical threats, all while standing next to our child. The situation continued despite the show being almost finished.

Most concerning was the complete lack of response from the venue. There was no visible staff or security presence in the amphitheater, and no intervention at any point. I was forced to leave one of our children alone and go into the corridor to try to find help, yet no assistance came. Even after the show ended, the aggressive behaviour continued and we left feeling unsafe.

The impact on our family was significant. Our children were frightened and distressed, and the rest of our day was affected by stress and anxiety after what should have been a normal family outing.

When we approached reception ourselves, we were told to stand in a queue and submit a complaint. This is not an appropriate response when guests have been threatened and children are involved. Later, we received an official reply describing the incident as a “misunderstanding.” We strongly disagree: physical threats, lack of intervention, and distressed children are not a misunderstanding.

We expect a formal follow-up from management and clear action to ensure visible staff and security presence, proper escalation procedures, and active monitoring during family shows. Without these measures, families cannot feel safe attending events at this venue.

name: SeaWorld Abu Dhabi | سي وورلد جزيرة ياس، أبوظ
review_text:
We liked this place overall.

The thing that bummed us the most about this place was the staff's behavior at the entry gate. They were checking bags and the checking lady in the extreme right line was super rude. She not only made us throw all food we had, but also spoke in a very condescending tone and humiliated us out of the queue.

I requested her to let us keep a piece of cake we got for our son, but NO, she asked us to throw that too. How else would food vendors inside the park earn if we get our son's favorite cake inside the park, even if it were to make sure he's not famished in the first half of the day.

I am all in for compliance and following rules, just be a little flexible when it comes to kids and a small piece of cake ain't hurting anybody. Toddlers are hard to console when something they're looking forward to, gets thrown in the bin.

Nevertheless, we started with the dolphin show. Very average. Kudos to the dolphins, but the stage presenters really need to up their game. No one could understand a word they said. The dolphin show at the Dubai Dolphinarium was wayyyyyyyyy better. Also, what's with the reserved seating at the auditorium ? You wouldn't give reserved seats to folks with toddlers even if they reach the auditorium well before the show, but quick pass owners get reserved seating even at the last minute? I understand quick pass folks getting quick access , but why give them reserved seating ?

Anyway, endless ocean and Arctic circle is beautifully maintained at Sea World. We loved the penguin area and how everybody gets a chance to get close to the penguins in a habitat that suits them.

Loved the Polar region too, the Walrus was the big showstopper at the park. Maybe do something about the stench in that area ?

Food at Seaworld is pretty expensive, but the café near the penguin area is particularly goood and has good value for money.

We missed the mermaid show and there was just 1 show in the entire day. It was a bummer to not have caught that show. Felt like there could be announcements in the park or displays that showed timings and venues to these things..

The amazing 360 displays at the center of the park enthrall you and present a spectacular view of the shows.

review_text:
Major safety failure: no staff or security response to threats during a family show

We attended a show here with our two children (aged 4 and 7). What happened raised serious concerns about guest safety and the venue’s ability to manage incidents inside the amphitheater.

Seating was unassigned and guests were taking any available seats. I entered first and seated our child in a single free seat. No one indicated that the seat was reserved or being held. When my husband arrived a few minutes later, he sat with our child (the child remained in the same seat, sitting on his lap). At that point, a nearby group suddenly claimed the seat was being held.

A man from that group arrived about a minute before the end of the show and immediately began shouting at my husband, claiming the seat and making direct physical threats, all while standing next to our child. The situation continued despite the show being almost finished.

Most concerning was the complete lack of response from the venue. There was no visible staff or security presence in the amphitheater, and no intervention at any point. I was forced to leave one of our children alone and go into the corridor to try to find help, yet no assistance came. Even after the show ended, the aggressive behaviour continued and we left feeling unsafe.

The impact on our family was significant. Our children were frightened and distressed, and the rest of our day was affected by stress and anxiety after what should have been a normal family outing.

When we approached reception ourselves, we were told to stand in a queue and submit a complaint. This is not an appropriate response when guests have been threatened and children are involved. Later, we received an official reply describing the incident as a “misunderstanding.” We strongly disagree: physical threats, lack of intervention, and distressed children are not a misunderstanding.

We expect a formal follow-up from management and clear action to ensure visible staff and security presence, proper escalation procedures, and active monitoring during family shows. Without these measures, families cannot feel safe attending events at this venue.

review_text:
We stayed here for 7 days, and it was the first holiday in a long time where I didn't want to go back home.

The hotel was phenomenal, both in staff and amenities. My previous experience in the UAE was Jumeriah Al Qasr Dubai, and this was even better. Lovely pools, amazing private beach, and wonderful interiors.

The staff were extremely helpful and attentive throughout our stay, going out of their way especially for our 1-year-old daughter. On one occasion a cleaner passed us in the hallway, asked for our room number, and then returned 10 minutes later with a toy for our baby. Such thoughtfulness means a lot when travelling with a family. Special mention to doorman Siju who helped us out repeatedly with our pram and car seat.

Food wise, I was absolutely blown away by the daily buffet. I am not normally a fan of this, but I have NEVER been to a buffet of such consistently high quality and variety. Unfortunately, I did eat too much and now need to diet. There was too much food to try and all of it was excellent.

This was such a great trip for our family, and my daughter also learned to walk in the long carpeted corridors outside the rooms.

In terms of location, it's ideally situated with a Souk on one side and a pier full of restaurants (and the aquarium) on the other. It's also a short Careem/Uber ride to the malls, which were also brilliant. There is a gym next to the Souk which does the job for anyone looking to burn some calories (machines for every body part, a smith machine, a trap bar, and some heavyish dumbells).

I will certainly be returning - much calmer than Dubai and far fewer influencers.

Thank you for an unforgettable stay.

review_text:
🌴

في كل مرة أزور فيها جزيرة صير بني ياس تكون الزيارة عن طريق الكروز، وهذه كانت المرة الثانية.
الجزيرة جميلة جدًا وبسيطة، وتتميز بطبيعتها الهادئة.
تضم بعض الحيوانات، وقد قمنا بتجربة سفاري بسيارات الجيب وكانت تجربة ممتعة ومميزة.
كما شاهدنا الدلافين، وكان منظرها جميلًا جدًا ومبهجًا.
تحتوي الجزيرة على أكثر من فندق، وتتوفر فيها العديد من الأنشطة مثل السباحة، الكاياك، الجت سكي وغيرها الكثير.
استمتعنا كثيرًا بالزيارة، وأنصح بها بشدة لكل من يبحث عن تجربة طبيعية وهادئة.

——

Every time I visit Sir Bani Yas Island, it is through a cruise, and this was my second visit.
The island is very beautiful, simple, and peaceful, with a relaxing natural atmosphere.
It is home to some wildlife, and we enjoyed an exciting jeep safari experience.
We also saw dolphins, and the view was absolutely beautiful and joyful.
The island features more than one hotel and offers many activities such as swimming, kayaking, jet skiing, and more.
We truly enjoyed the visit and highly recommend it to anyone looking for a calm and nature-filled getaway.

review_text:
تعتبر جزيرة صير بني ياس واحدة من المواقع الثمانية التي تشكل جزر الصحراء في منطقة الظفرة إذ تتميّز بواجهتها الطبيعية البرية والأنشطة الشيّقة التي تقدّمها والفنادق والفلل الفاخرة بالإضافة إلى الاسطبلات والمواقع التاريخية استثنائية.
حصدت الجزيرة جائزة أفضل وجهة سياحية مستدامة في العالم ضمن جوائز السفر العالمية 2014، حيث تضمّ منتزه الحياة البرية العربية الذي يُعدّ أحد أكبر محميات الحياة البرية في المنطقة إذ يشمل أكثر من 17 ألف حيوان مثل المها العربي والغزلان والزرافات والضباع والفهود الصيادة. يتسنى للضيوف أيضاً الاستمتاع بجولة في سيارة رباعية الدفع لاستكشاف الطبيعة والحياة البرية برفقة فريق من الخبراء فيما توفر اسطبلات الجزيرة الحديثة مجموعةً متنوعة من أنشطة الفروسية ودروس ركوب الخيل لجميع أفراد العائلة. وإذا كنت ترغب في الانطلاق بجولة استكشافية في الجزيرة، يستطيع منتجع دانات جبل الظنة الواقع في البر الرئيسي لأبوظبي مساعدتك في حجز جولة.

وتضم جزيرة صير بني ياس الدير المسيحي الوحيد الذي تمّ اكتشافه في دولة الإمارات العربية المتّحدة والذي يمكن زيارته أثناء جولات منتجع وسبا جزر الصحراء السياحية. ويُعتقدُ بأنّ الدير بُنِي حوالى العام 600 م، ثمّ تمّ هجره في العام 750 م. أمّا اكتشافه فتمّ خلال عمليات التنقيب في الجزيرة في العام 1992.

name: Sir Baniyas Island
review_text:
We stayed for three nights as part of the inaugural Challenge Sir Bani Yas event.

The island itself quite a drive away. 3:30hrs from Dubai 2hrs from Abu Dhabi.

There is a private airport if that’s how you roll.

To get to the island otherwise you need to take a ferry. You must pre book and provide identification. The journey itself is around 30mins or less.

The island has been invested in by the Abu Dhabi government. The roads are good and so is signage etc.

We stayed in the Anantara (the only option) the staff are amazing. Facilities though are definitely aged. Still nice but nothing compared to other Anantara resorts.

The safari is not like a Kenyan safari. At the time of writing this there is one zebra and two cheetahs. Both of which were hiding at the back of a cage when we were there. Giraffes are amazing though and they have plenty of other wildlife. Over 13000.

Two nights is more than enough.

review_text:
A definite one time visit to understand and appreciate the vision of the country; the island is aimed at planting trees and increasing fertility of its land so as to make it an agricultural area. Very wide spread area with animals running around and well maintained.

The trip from Abu Dhabi to the ferry took 2.30 hours. The ferry ride is another 30 minutes ride and then a bus that will take you to the Anantara resort from where the Safari for wildlife begins. The safari is a 90 minute ride with a tour guide. Very passionate tour guides and makes it a wonderful experience.

The journey can get tiring if you take a day visit; like we did. There is quite a lot of journey involved. It’s worth the visit at least once. Please take snacks and water with you so that you are not starving. Although the safari ride do have water in their cars. The safari cars are quite comfortable as well; and they help seniors get into the vehicle with additional support if they aren’t able to get into the jeep.

Good place to go with family; I would recommend a stay though in the hotel. If you have a tight budget; just take a day visit and enjoy nature at its diversity! Start with a full tank and then there are petrol stations almost when you reach Sir baniyas

query: sir-bani-yas,Sir Bani Yas Island, Sir Bani Yas Island, Abu Dhabi
name: Sir Baniyas Island
review_text:
Beautiful experience overall. The grounds, flora, and fauna that they’ve managed to create is stunning as the place is generally not highly fertile. The project is very ambitious. On the Sir Bani Yas island there are 3 resorts. One feels like another hotel is Dubai or Abu Dhabi, that’s (1) Desert Islands Resort & Spa, (2) Sahel Villa Resort, and (3) Al Yamm Villa Resort. They have cars on the island shuttling you around from one resort to another one so that you can try the different restaurants so no need to worry about not having enough dining options. For context, we stayed at Al Yamm Villa Resort.

Here is the good, the bad, and special:

The ‘Good’
- The resort felt rustic and it fit in the environment
- The private villa’s pool was heated so it was comfy to get into at night
- Turn down service was nice. They have yummy cookies
- Even though they take a bit of time to reply, the Anantara app is useful to connect with front desk
- You get access to the beautiful beach
- There are different activities to keep the fun going

The ‘Bad’
- We paid AED 5,000 per night and AED 1,000+ per meal and we felt the value wasn’t there versus Nurai Island or Al Maha Resort
- The villa is definitely outdated. I love that it’s rustic, but it can definitely use an upgrade asap. For the prices they charge, it should be luxurious
- We wanted a king size bed and they gave us 2 queens and pushed the beds together :( Even though the beds were comfortable, we aren’t used to sleeping on anything less than a California King
- Privacy of the outdoor area of the villa was lacking in a major way. Not only could your neighbors see you 100% at all times, but even people walking in front of the villas
- Reception doesn’t welcome you with useful information about the resort and how things work
- Hit or miss when it came to the staff knowing English well
- The shower head holder of the villa was loose. Housekeeping should check for all these things and get them fixed before the guest arrives.
- Getting the shower head to work was impossible
- The amenities in the bathroom lacked a loofah
- The transportation boat from the mainland to the island and return was simply awful. They should have a high quality boat just for guests staying at the hotel(s) on the island

The ‘Special’

- Tour guide of the mini safari was amazing. Very knowledgeable and cared a lot about the island itself as a project
- Dinner at the African restaurant in the Sahel property was special. They had some nice music on the background coming from the ‘bush’ and it made it cozy
- At the African restaurant, baby oryx approached and it was a beautiful experience
- The spa was solid. We had a couples experience which included time in the jacuzzi, then a massage, and mini facials
- The animal variety in the mini safari tour was great. I’m still amazed at what they were able to build here

Would I go back?
- Yes, I hope they fix all these things, but regardless I’d love to go back and experience it with friends and family

review_text:
Das Wahat Al Karama Monument ist den Märtyrern der vereinigten Arabischen Emirate gewidmet, und ehrt die Taten der Kriegshelden, die ihr Leben für das Wohlergehen der Bürger der vereinigten Arabischen Emirate opferten. Das kostenlos zugängliche Monument, ist nachts beleuchtet, und ein Superfoto Spot für die große Moschee, die sich direkt gegenüber befindet.

Benötigte Besuchszeit : für die Besichtigung des Monuments, und die ebenfalls auf dem Gelände befindliche Kunstausstellung, sollten Besucher 30-45 Minuten einplanen.

Anreise: es gibt eine Fußgängerbrücke, die von der großen Moschee direkt rüber zu dem Monument führt, wodurch das Wahat Al Karama Monument einfach zu Fuß erreicht werden kann. Es stehen jedoch auch ausreichend kostenlose Parkplätze zur Verfügung, und für die Anreise mit dem öffentlichen Nahverkehr, gibt es eine Bushaltestelle, die sich ebenfalls direkt vor dem Monument befindet.

Shuttle Bus: es gibt einen Shuttle Bus, der im 30 Minuten Takt zwischen dem Wahat Al Karama Monument, und der großen Moschee hin und her fährt.

Eintritt: Das Wahat Al Karama Monument ist 24/7 kostenlos zugänglich, und Barriere frei!

review_text:
Of course. Here is an extremely positive review for Wahat Al Karama, written specifically for photographers.

★★★★★

The Ultimate Reflection Shot of the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque!

For photographers, Wahat Al Karama isn't just a beautiful memorial; it is the single best and most essential location in Abu Dhabi for capturing an iconic, postcard-perfect shot of the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque.

The key is the massive, shallow reflection pool that forms the centerpiece of the memorial. It is a perfectly designed, giant liquid mirror. By positioning yourself at the far end of the pool, you can achieve a breathtaking, symmetrical reflection of the entire mosque, including all its domes and minarets.

The best time to shoot is unquestionably sunset. Arrive about an hour before sunset to secure your spot. You'll be able to capture the mosque during the golden hour as the warm light hits its white marble, then witness the sky explode with color, and finally, stay for the magical blue hour as the mosque's own lights turn on, creating a dazzling display in both the sky and the water.

Bring a tripod, a wide-angle lens, and some patience. The shot you will walk away with is absolutely world-class and worth the visit alone. A must-do for any serious cityscape or travel photographer visiting Abu Dhabi.
